items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I also wrote to my friend Hans Bluthner in Berlin and told him that Lily would be coming there at a certain date and ask him to help her in what every way he possibly could.

ctx.x: I had an interview at the TV and di a concert the 29th with some very good German musicians after only talking over a few numbers I wanted to play. The public was very enthusiastic and I had a great reception.

After the concert, I was invited to the most popular jazz club in Berlin, so I was told. It was the largest jazz club I had seen in Europe. It could hold about 400 people. Hans, Fritz and Tiger Jones went with me. Jones was a jazz fan as so many athletes are. There was a fine guitarist whom I met, named Rediske and I sat in with his group and the joint was really swinging. Tiger Jones could sing and not bad, so he joined the session also. He was well known there because when he was not in training, he was in this…

As this was my first time in Berlin, Hans and Fritz took me out sight-seeing the 30th. The effects of the bombings that Berlin suffered in World War II could be seen everywhere, but the bricks from the ruins were stacked in neat piles and the streets were the cleanest I've ever seen anywhere. I saw the gateway to East Berlin, the Russian war memorial and the stadium where Hitler had refused to shake hands with the great American Negro athlete Jessie Owens during the 1936 Olympic Games.
